statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON (green). Tail 5% (low), Stress 38% (moderate), Confidence 88% (high). Market halted for the full horizon.
recommendation: Tail is at a closed-market floor and the mapped policy state is EA_ON. No danger window is published because no venue quotes at any point in this horizon, so there is no evidence-based interval to flag. The relevant forward checkpoint sits outside the window: the Sunday 22:00 UTC futures reopen, where weekend developments in the US-Iran conflict and any shift in September Fed pricing would be expressed as a single gap rather than as an observable path. Existing-position management and emergency protection remain unaffected by the mapped state, and the next assessment cycles will score the reopen once a live price path exists.
headline: Nasdaq-100 closes the payroll week at 29,544.15 after an orderly two-way session; with futures settled at 21:00 UTC the whole horizon is a halted venue and Tail sits at a closed-market floor
body: The Nasdaq-100 finished the August payroll session at 29,544.15, up 0.21% from a 29,482.32 prior close, after opening at 29,539.57, extending to 29,655.22, fully retracing that advance to a 29,440.15 low and recovering into the cash close. Retracements occurred repeatedly in both directions, which is the opposite of the persistent no-retracement structure the Tail score measures. CME equity index futures then settled at 21:00 UTC, so as of this assessment there is no live price path for either NQ futures or the NAS100 CFD, and none will exist until the Sunday 22:00 UTC reopen. Monday 7 September is the US Labor Day holiday. Volatility confirmed the orderly reading: VIX closed at 14.53, up 1.47%, inside a 13.80-14.58 range. The August employment report, verified at the BLS release, printed 162,000 nonfarm payrolls against roughly 53,000-55,000 expected, unemployment steady at 4.1% and average hourly earnings up 0.3% on the month to $37.75 and 3.1% over the year. Rate transmission stayed contained rather than disorderly: the 10-year yield rose 2.2 basis points to 4.784% inside a 4.748-4.812 range, while the 2-year traded near 4.42%, its highest since January 2025, with September hike pricing around 58% ahead of the 15-16 September FOMC. The H.15 release still shows 3 September as its latest official column at 4.34% and 4.77%. Energy remains the live geopolitical channel: WTI settled at $91.48, up 0.20%, and Brent at $92.68, up 0.8%, for weekly gains near 10% and 7.6% as US-Iran hostilities resumed, Strait of Hormuz transits ran far below normal and US diesel reached a record $5.85 per gallon. Delayed shared cross-asset context, used only as supporting evidence, showed the same dispersion rather than one-way index structure: semiconductors were uniformly higher, led by Micron, AMD, Intel and Arm, while Tesla, Apple, Microsoft and Alphabet were lower, and latest-session futures had NQ marginally positive against weaker ES and YM. That combination is a rotation signature, not the aligned single-direction stack that would justify a raised Tail. With the venue halted for the entire 24-hour horizon, Tail is published at a closed-market floor of 5%, while Stress at 38% represents unpriced weekend exposure to active Middle East escalation and firmer Fed pricing rather than any observed drawdown.

lookbackSummary: The prior 24 hours span the calm pre-payroll regime, the August employment release and its decay into the Friday cash close and futures settlement. Tail drifted from 14% down to 12% and back to 17% through the Asian and European sessions while Stress climbed steadily from 53% to 62% into the print. The 12:00 UTC hour carried the only genuine spike, with Tail at 24%, Stress at 76% and Confidence down to 74% as event/whipsaw conditions took over on the 162,000 payroll surprise. Price discovery then proved orderly: the initial move was retraced, Tail fell to 20% and 18% over the next two hours and back into the low teens through the US afternoon, with dominant mode moving from event/whipsaw to mixed as semiconductor strength offset megacap weakness. The published series stayed at EA_ON and green for 22 of the 24 hours, with WATCH and yellow only in the two hours immediately around the release.
outlookSummary: The entire 24-hour horizon falls inside the weekend halt. CME equity index futures settled at 21:00 UTC and do not reopen until 22:00 UTC on Sunday 6 September, roughly 25 hours after this horizon ends, and Monday 7 September is the US Labor Day holiday. Because no venue quotes during any published hour, the pathological price path that Tail measures cannot form, so forecast Tail is held at a 4-5% closed-market floor and the dominant mode of normal denotes a halted rather than a directional regime. Stress is held in the mid-30s and drifts marginally higher through Saturday to reflect weekend information accumulating unpriced against active US-Iran hostilities and firmer September Fed pricing; that exposure is real for anything held through the break but is expressed as a single reopen gap rather than as a tradable path. Confidence decays gradually from 88% to 80% purely with distance from the verified Friday evidence cutoff. No macro release falls inside the horizon; the next verified checkpoints are PPI on 10 September and CPI on 11 September, both at 12:30 UTC, ahead of the 15-16 September FOMC.
